record.original_question: Is termination decidable for a single rewrite rule that is both left-linear and right-linear? Relatedly, what is known about decidability of termination or confluence for one monadic or non-monadic string rewrite rule?

evidence.quote: Is termination of one linear rule decidable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider term rewriting systems over a finite signature with variables. A rewrite rule l → r is left-linear if no variable occurs more than once in l, and right-linear if no variable occurs more than once in r; the rule is called linear if it is both left-linear and right-linear. A rewrite system terminates if there is no infinite rewrite sequence t₁ → t₂ → t₃ → ⋯ using its rules.

Question: Is termination decidable for a single linear rewrite rule, i.e., does there exist an algorithm that, given any rule l → r in which every variable occurs at most once on each side, decides whether the one-rule rewrite system {l → r} terminates?

Related questions in the same spirit: Is termination (respectively, confluence) decidable for a single string (semi-Thue) rewrite rule l → r, in either the monadic case (where r has length at most one over the alphabet) or the general non-monadic case?
artifact.status_search_result: Termination of one-rule term/string rewriting is a long-standing open problem. Undecidability is known for one rule that is only left-linear (Dauchet's simulation of Turing machines by a left-linear one-rule system), but the linear (both left- and right-linear) one-rule case, as well as the one-rule string rewriting case, remain open. Various partial decidability results exist for restricted subclasses (e.g., single-threaded systems, growing systems, rules with restricted overlaps), but no general algorithm is known.

status_evidence.title: Simulation of Turing machines by a left-linear rewrite rule
status_evidence.snippet: Dauchet shows undecidability of termination for one left-linear rule, but linear (both sides) and one-rule string rewriting cases remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Termination of one left-linear rule is undecidable; the linear case and one-rule string case are not settled here.

status_evidence.title: Termination of String Rewriting Rules That Have One Pair of Overlaps
status_evidence.snippet: Partial solution to the long standing open problem whether termination of one-rule string rewriting is decidable.
status_evidence.claim: Decidability of termination for one string rewriting rule is described as a long-standing open problem.

status_evidence.title: RTA List of Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: List of open problems in rewriting, including decidability of termination/confluence for single rules.
status_evidence.claim: The community maintains these as open problems.
